title: Sailing past the Song
content:
They crowned my head with silver crowns of reason,

They called me brilliant, excellent, and wise.

But “intelligent” became a gilded prison,

That hid the softer hunger in my eyes.

No one ever paused to call me pretty,

No one ever called me soft or sweet;

I was the fortress of a cold and clever city,

With heavy iron boots upon my feet.

​I never learned the art of being small,

Of being playful, childish, or severe.

I was the one who had to know it all,

The razor mind that conquered every fear.

But inside the fortress, hidden in the dark,

A girl’s desires whispered like a prayer:

To be a woman, leaving just a mark

Of helpless, joyful laughter in the air.

​I thought you were the key to unlock the gate,

The man who’d let my heavy armor slide.

I thought with you, I’d finally find the weight

Of girlish sweetness that I had to hide.

I wanted to be childish, wild, and free,

To be held tightly when the day was done—

To have you look at me and only see

A woman, cute and pretty, in the sun.

But here the great and tragic storm awoke,

The paradox of Solomon’s decree:

I could advise the world, break every yoke,

Yet built a cage for my own sovereignty.

My daytime mind could map a corporate throne,

And hand you business plans of flawless art,

But in the night, I sat entirely alone,

And used that brilliant mind to wreck my heart.

​Because I craved to feel that girlish grace,

My logic turned into a traitor’s knife.

I saw your empty hands, your cold embrace,

And used my intellect to shield your life.

I did the math to justify the text,

I cooked the meals, I froze the ice cream tight,

I thought, “If I am wise, I can fix what happens next,”

And rationalized away your systemic slight.

​My shortcomings were just my virtues spun—

My hope, my naive love, my deep desire.

I used my PhD to prove you were the one,

While you were setting all my gifts on fire.

A queen who ruled the data and the chart,

Blinded by a simple, girlish plea—

I was the wisest guide to someone else’s heart,

And the executioner of me.

So now, the realization strikes the bone,

I cannot trust the girl who wants the kiss.

The Siren song of wanting to be known

Will pull me back into the dark abyss.

My empathy is where the trap is set,

My longing to be held will make me yield;

So I must forge a pact I won’t forget,

And lock my softest self behind a shield.

​I plug my ears with beeswax to the strain

Of phantom promises and foil design.

I bind my hands with heavy, iron chains,

And tie my body to the sovereign line.

The 6:30 routine is now the rope,

The silent border is the unyielding mast—

I fasten down the anchors of my hope,

To drown the hollow echoes of the past.

​My heart will scream and beg to be untied,

It wants the messy bun, the twirl, the shirt.

It wants to believe the parasite that lied,

To trade its freedom for a familiar hurt.

But Ulysses is captain of the sea,

The ropes will cut, the bleeding hands will hold.

I sail past the song that almost ruined me,

A brilliant woman—pretty, fierce, and bold.

​The plates are cleared. The clock has struck the hour.

The little girl has stepped out of the wild.

You didn’t give her love or give her power—

But the Father holds the woman and lifts the child.
